<description>
Guix release binaries use GCC’s POSIX thread model, while the pinned Nixpkgs toolchain defaults to mcf. This makes POSIX the default for Nix Windows cross builds. Nightly builds can select `mcf` or `win32` with the `threadModel` argument.

The Nixpkgs `threads` setting selects the model before GCC is built. Only the mcf model pulls in `mcfgthreads`. For POSIX, GCC’s target libraries need winpthreads headers and libraries during the compiler build. The `EXTRA_*_FOR_TARGET` flags provide those paths without exposing target headers to GCC’s native build tools, which caused the earlier build failure.

The compiler wrapper includes winpthreads through `extraPackages`, so the shell no longer needs to export pthread include and library flags manually. CI also prints GCC’s configured thread model to make mismatches visible.

Fixes #36314
</description>

[2026-09-23] c:5794718936 comment by willcl-ark (member):
Hmmm, we are starting to veer into quite a lot of extra code needed to support this on-the-fly switching:

```patch
commit 78331095c68b8df4cf34f3b7b761506af6239915
Author: will <will@256k1.dev>
Date:   Wed Sep 23 13:06:56 2026 +0100

    ci: expose winpthreads for all Windows thread models

    ZeroMQ includes pthread.h even when GCC uses the MCF thread model.
    The POSIX-only wrapper exposed winpthreads, so MCF builds failed
    despite GCC itself selecting mcf successfully.

    Add winpthreads to every wrapper while retaining mcfgthreads for MCF.
    Keep the target-only GCC build flags specific to POSIX, where GCC needs
    them while building its runtime libraries.

diff --git a/contrib/devtools/shell-win64-cross.nix b/contrib/devtools/shell-win64-cross.nix
index f61d3e93497..8b22d55ebbf 100644
--- a/contrib/devtools/shell-win64-cross.nix
+++ b/contrib/devtools/shell-win64-cross.nix
@@ -25,20 +25,20 @@ let
   toolchain = crossPkgs.stdenv.cc.targetPrefix;
   pthreads = crossPkgs.windows.pthreads;
   crossGcc = crossPkgs.buildPackages.gcc14;
-  gcc = if threadModel == "posix" then
-    crossGcc.override {
-      cc = crossGcc.cc.overrideAttrs (old: {
-        # Keep target pthread headers out of GCC's native build tools.
-        env = old.env // {
-          EXTRA_FLAGS_FOR_TARGET =
-            "${old.env.EXTRA_FLAGS_FOR_TARGET} -idirafter ${pthreads}/include -B${pthreads}/lib";
-          EXTRA_LDFLAGS_FOR_TARGET =
-            "${old.env.EXTRA_LDFLAGS_FOR_TARGET} -Wl,-L${pthreads}/lib";
-        };
-      });
-      extraPackages = [ pthreads ];
-    }
-  else crossGcc;
+  gcc = crossGcc.override {
+    cc = if threadModel == "posix" then crossGcc.cc.overrideAttrs (old: {
+      # Keep target pthread headers out of GCC's native build tools.
+      env = old.env // {
+        EXTRA_FLAGS_FOR_TARGET =
+          "${old.env.EXTRA_FLAGS_FOR_TARGET} -idirafter ${pthreads}/include -B${pthreads}/lib";
+        EXTRA_LDFLAGS_FOR_TARGET =
+          "${old.env.EXTRA_LDFLAGS_FOR_TARGET} -Wl,-L${pthreads}/lib";
+      };
+    }) else crossGcc.cc;
+    # ZeroMQ needs pthread.h even when GCC uses a different thread model.
+    extraPackages =
+      [ pthreads ] ++ pkgs.lib.optional (threadModel == "mcf") crossPkgs.threads.package;
+  };
 in
```
